prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1087; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed collision in a retail parking lot. Insured reports the other vehicle backed into the driver's side rear quarter panel. Both drivers exchanged information at the scene and police were not called. Photos of both vehicles requested from insured.

Entry 2: Received photos and a written statement from insured. Damage appears limited to the rear bumper cover and left taillight assembly on the insured vehicle. Claimant vehicle shows scuffing and a cracked reflector on the front passenger bumper. Liability appears probable against the other driver, pending witness review.

Entry 3: Claimant has reported neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash. Claimant is now represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office per company protocol. Medical authorization and records request sent to counsel. No direct contact with claimant from this point forward.

Entry 4: Counsel's office provided initial treatment notes showing evaluation, imaging referral, and a course of physical therapy. Treating provider has noted a diagnosis of cervical strain. Bodily injury evaluation has been referred to the medical review unit. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect the injury component.

Entry 5: Medical review unit returned preliminary notes. Records are consistent with the reported mechanism of injury, though treatment duration is being reviewed. Counsel has been advised that a settlement position will follow once the review is complete. Property damage estimate finalized and sent to the other carrier for subrogation. File remains open pending medical review.
